| {{flag|Mexico}} || {{dts|5 February 2025}}<ref name="avmedia">{{Cite AV media |url=https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2025/02/05/mexico/video/sheinbaum-palestina-israel-estados-conflicto-orix-perspectivas-mexico-tv |title=Sheinbaum ratifica que México reconoce a Palestina e Israel como Estados y pide una salida pacífica del conflicto |date=5 February 2025 |last=Ledesma |first=Araceli |language=es |publisher=CNN en Español |trans-title=Sheinbaum confirms that Mexico recognizes Palestine and Israel as states and calls for a peaceful solution to the conflict. |access-date=21 March 2025 |via=cnnespanol.cnn.com}}</ref>|| {{Yes}}<ref name="El Heraldo">{{Cite web |date=20 March 2025 |title=Histórico: reconoce México al Estado de Palestina |trans-title=Historic: Mexico recognizes the State of Palestine |url=https://elheraldoslp.com.mx/new/2025/03/20/historico-reconoce-mexico-al-estado-de-palestina/ |access-date=22 March 2025 |website=El Heraldo |language=es}}</ref> || G20, OAS; [[Mexico–Palestine relations]]
{{show
|Further details
|Mexico was listed in documents circulated at the United Nations in 2024 as having recognized Palestine on 2 June 2023,<ref name="documents.un.org"/> the same date that the State of Palestine announced the conversion of its "Special Delegation" in Mexico into an "Embassy" without specifying whether that was by agreement with the Mexican government.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sánchez Jiménez |first1=Arturo |title=Reclasifica Palestina misión diplomática en México; abrirá embajada |url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/notas/2023/06/02/politica/reclasifica-palestina-mision-diplomatica-en-mexico-abrira-embajada/?from=homeonline&block=ultimasnoticias |access-date=20 October 2025 |work=La Jornada |date=2 June 2023}}</ref> The State of Palestine was reportedly soon added to a list of embassies in Mexico on a Mexican government website,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hackbarth |first1=Kurt |title=Mexico Has Fully Recognized the State of Palestine |url=https://jacobin.com/2023/07/mexico-amlo-israel-palestine-embassy-diplomacy |access-date=19 October 2025 |work=Jacobin |date=5 July 2023}}</ref> and at least one source would later credit Mexican president [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] with having affected the change.<ref name="SheinbaumRasheed">{{cite news |title=Sheinbaum welcomes Palestinian Ambassador Nadya Rasheed |url=https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/mexicos-sheinbaum-welcomes-palestinian-ambassador-nadya-rasheed/ |access-date=19 October 2025 |work=Mexico News Daily |date=24 March 2025}}</ref> In a press release from 25 April 2024, the Mexican government stated that "Mexico has supported actions in several multilateral forums that have, among others, the legal effect of recognizing Palestine as a State.",<ref>{{cite web |author1=Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores |title=Mexico reaffirms its support for Palestine to become a full member of the United Nations |url=https://www.gob.mx/sre/prensa/mexico-reaffirms-its-support-for-palestine-to-become-a-full-member-of-the-united-nations?idiom=en |website=Gobierno de México |access-date=19 October 2025 |date=25 April 2024}}</ref> and on 11 October 2024 Mexican President [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] said "we believe that the Palestinian State should be recognized in its full scope, just like the State of Israel."<ref>{{cite news |title=Versión estenográfica. Conferencia de prensa de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo del 11 de octubre de 2024 |url=https://www.gob.mx/presidencia/articulos/version-estenografica-conferencia-de-prensa-de-la-presidenta-claudia-sheinbaum-pardo-del-11-de-octubre-de-2024?idiom=es |access-date=19 October 2025 |agency=Gobierno de México |date=11 October 2024}}</ref> On 5 February 2025 Sheinbaum stated that "Mexico has had a position since years ago, not only of the governments of the [[Fourth Transformation]], but it comes from before, of recognition of the State of Palestine and at the same time of the State of Israel. So that is the policy of the Mexican government of years ago and of now."<ref name="avmedia" /><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://oem.com.mx/elsoldemexico/mexico/sheinbaum-reitera-posicion-de-mexico-para-encontrar-salida-pacifica-en-gaza-21541974 |title=México reconoce al Estado Palestino, dice Sheinbaum tras propuesta de Trump de tomar control en Gaza |date=5 February 2025 |last=Cabrera |first=Atzayacatl |language=es |publisher=[[El Sol de México]] |trans-title=Mexico recognizes the Palestinian state, Sheinbaum says, after Trump's proposal to take control of Gaza. |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref> Some media outlets reported that Mexico recognized Palestine on 19 March 2025<ref name="El Heraldo" /> in reference to the accreditation ceremony for the first Palestinian representative to Mexico under the title of "Ambassador".<ref name="SheinbaumRasheed" />}}

| {{flag|Austria}} || Austria conferred full diplomatic status on the PLO representation in Vienna on 13 December 1978, under then-chancellor [[Bruno Kreisky]].<ref name="quigley2010">{{cite book |last=Quigley |first=John B. |title=The statehood of Palestine: international law in the Middle East conflict |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iTR3BQ0aJ6UC |page=151 |year=2010 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-15165-8}}</ref> In June 2011, Foreign Minister [[Michael Spindelegger]] said that Austria "had not yet made up its mind whether to support a UN recognition of a Palestinian state", adding that he preferred to wait for a joint EU approach to the issue. He said: "We will decide at the last moment because it might still give [the two parties] the opportunity to bring the Middle East peace process back on track."<ref>{{cite web |last=Salam |first=Kawther |title=Lieberman Came To Vienna And Brought Us A Storm |url=http://www.kawther.info/wpr/2011/07/01/lieberman-came-to-vienna-and-brought-us-a-storm |date=1 July 2011 |access-date=1 August 2011 |archive-date=12 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181112141401/http://www.kawther.info/wpr/2011/07/01/lieberman-came-to-vienna-and-brought-us-a-storm |url-status=live }}</ref> Spindelegger also suggested that the EU draft its own version of the resolution.<ref name="yahoo">{{cite news |title=Plan B on Palestine at the UN? Europeans mull alternative resolution |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/blogs/envoy/plan-b-palestine-un-europeans-mull-alternative-resolution-191706340.html |date=2 September 2011 |publisher=Yahoo! News |access-date=12 October 2017 |archive-date=13 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171013014747/https://www.yahoo.com/news/blogs/envoy/plan-b-palestine-un-europeans-mull-alternative-resolution-191706340.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2025, the Federal Chancellery of [[Christian Stocker]] stated that "many steps still lie ahead of recognition".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wie halten es Europas Länder mit der Anerkennung Palästinas? |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/3000000288269/wie-halten-es-europas-laender-mit-der-anerkennung-palaestinas |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=DER STANDARD |language=de-AT}}</ref>
{{show
|Further details
|
Austria was initially listed as having recognized the State of Palestine on 14 December 1988, in documents submitted to UNESCO in 1989 supporting to Palestine's application for membership. However, the submitting states (Algeria, Indonesia, Mauritania, Nigeria, Senegal and Yemen) later requested that Austria be removed from the list.<ref name="unesco"/>}}
| Yes<ref>{{cite web |date=1 September 1980 |title=Die Anerkennung der PLO durch Österreich |trans-title=Recognition of the PLO by Austria |url=http://www.zaoerv.de/40_1980/40_1980_4_b_841_857.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041458/http://www.zaoerv.de/40_1980/40_1980_4_b_841_857.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=7 May 2011 |language=de}}</ref>|| EU; [[Austria–Palestine relations]]

|website=vrtnws.be}}</ref> while Prime Minister [[Alexander De Croo]] stressed that recognition was "symbolic" and would not have "any impact in the field".<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 May 2024 | {{flag|Cameroon}} || Cameroon officially supports a two-state solution.<ref name="cameroon-info">{{cite news |author=Noah Awana |first=Alain |date=3 November 2011 |title=La Palestine admise à l'UNESCO: Le Cameroun refuse de se prononcer |trans-title=Palestine admitted to UNESCO: Cameroon refuses to comment |url=http://www.cameroon-info.net/article/la-palestine-admise-a-lunesco-le-cameroun-refuse-de-se-prononcer-134868.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014034928/http://www.cameroon-info.net/article/la-palestine-admise-a-lunesco-le-cameroun-refuse-de-se-prononcer-134868.html |archive-date=14 October 2017 |access-date=13 October 2017 |publisher=Cameroon-Info |language=fr}}</ref> Although a member of the OIC, President [[Paul Biya]] has developed strong ties with Israel since the mid-1980s.<ref>{{cite book |last=Peters |first=Joel |title=Israel and Africa: the problematic friendship |publisher=I.B. Tauris |year=1992 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/israelafricap00pete/page/134 134–5] |isbn=978-1-870915-10-6 |url=https://archive.org/details/israelafricap00pete/page/134 }}</ref> This perceived friendship has soured the country's traditionally close ties with Arab states, many of whom have withdrawn longstanding economic development assistance and pressed Biya to support Palestinian interests.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Coplin |first1=W.D. |last2=O'Leary |first2=Michael |title=Political Risk Yearbook: 1990 |publisher=Cedar Tree House |year=1990 |isbn=978-1-85271-123-8}}</ref> In August 2011, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu asked Biya to oppose the UN resolution that would admit Palestine as a member state.<ref>{{cite news |last=Teke |first=Elvis |title=President Paul BIYA receives special message from Israeli Prime Minister |url=http://www.crtv.cm/cont/nouvelles/nouvelles_sola_fr.php?idField=9912&table=nouvelles&sub=national |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120729043007/http://www.crtv.cm/cont/nouvelles/nouvelles_sola_fr.php?idField=9912&table=nouvelles&sub=national |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 July 2012 |date=25 August 2011 |publisher=Cameroon Radio Television |access-date=19 September 2011 }}</ref>|| Yes<ref name="cameroon-info" />|| AU, OIC<ref name="erekat" />

| {{flag|Croatia}} || Croatia formalized relations with the [[Palestine Liberation Organization|PLO]] on 31 March 2011. Former Croatian Prime Minister [[Jadranka Kosor]] stated in 2011 that her government supported the co-existence of Israel and Palestine as two independent states;<ref>{{cite news |author=Government of Croatia |title=Croatia to formalise relations with Palestinians |url=http://www.vlada.hr/en/naslovnica/novosti_i_najave/2011/ozujak/hrvatska_formalizira_odnose_s_palestincima |publisher=News and Announcements |date=31 March 2011 |access-date=29 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928022241/http://www.vlada.hr/en/naslovnica/novosti_i_najave/2011/ozujak/hrvatska_formalizira_odnose_s_palestincima |archive-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> however, Croatia abstained during voting on [[United Nations General Assembly resolution 67/19|upgrading Palestine to non-member observer state status in the UN and on admission of Palestine to UNESCO]]. Former Croatian Foreign Minister [[Vesna Pusić]] stated on 24 October 2014 that "Croatia will most likely recognize Palestine soon".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-4583900,00.html |title=Croatia 'likely' to recognize Palestinian state |work=ynet |date=25 October 2014 |access-date=16 June 2015 |archive-date=16 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716014357/http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-4583900,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The Croatian government tends to favour Israel over Palestine as a commitment to the U.S., to whom Croatia is aligned, and the central quarters of the [[European Union]] of which Croatia has been a member since 2013. Croatia believes that if it were to recognize Palestine, this would frustrate its position with the EU and ties to the U.S., and also because the situation in the Middle East is complicated it feels there is no guarantee that there would be peace and further existence of the Jewish state if Israel eventually decides to withdraw from the [[Israeli-occupied territories|occupied territories]].<ref>{{cite news |date=28 June 2011 |title=Hrvatsko 'NE' Palestincima |trans-title=Croatian 'NO' to the Palestinians |url=http://arhiva.nacional.hr/clanak/111139/hrvatsko-ne-palestincima |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216141734/http://arhiva.nacional.hr/clanak/111139/hrvatsko-ne-palestincima |archive-date=16 February 2016 |access-date=18 August 2015 |website=Nacional.hr |language=Croatian}}</ref> In June 2025, President [[Zoran Milanović]] stated that Croatia should recognize Palestine.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 June 2025 |title=President Milanović: Croatia should recognize Palestine, and Israel wants to provoke a global conflict violently |url=https://www.predsjednik.hr/en/news/president-milanovic-croatia-should-recognize-palestine-and-israel-wants-to-provoke-a-global-conflict-violently/ |website=President of Croatia |access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref> On 27 August 2025, Milanović declared that he will vigorously push for Croatia to recognize Palestine as soon as feasible within the bounds of his constitutional authority. He is also urging the government to start the process of recognizing Palestine in the [[Croatian Parliament]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 August 2025 |title=President Milanović Is Calling on the Government of the Republic of Croatia to Initiate the Procedure to Recognize Palestine in the Croatian Parliament |url=https://www.predsjednik.hr/en/news/president-milanovic-is-calling-on-the-government-of-the-republic-of-croatia-to-initiate-the-procedure-to-recognize-palestine-in-the-croatian-parliament/ |website=President of Croatia |access-date=28 August 2025}}</ref> On 26 September 2025, a parliamentary motion to recognise Palestine, introduced by the political platform [[We Can! (Croatia)|We Can!]], was rejected by the governing majority led by the [[Croatian Democratic Union]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=croatiaweek |date=2025-09-26 |title=Croatian Parliament rejects immediate recognition of Palestine in vote |url=https://www.croatiaweek.com/croatian-parliament-rejects-immediate-recognition-of-palestine-in-vote/ |access-date=2026-05-02 |website=Croatia Week |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hrvatska se izjasnila protiv priznanja Palestine. Donosimo kako je tko glasao |url=https://www.index.hr/clanak.aspx?id=2713793 |access-date=2026-05-02 |website=www.index.hr |language=hr}}</ref>|| Yes || EU, NATO
|-
| {{flag|Denmark}} || Danish Foreign Minister [[Lene Espersen]] met Abbas on 9 March 2011 to persuade him to return to negotiating with Israel. Espersen also extended Danish support to Palestinian national development.<ref>{{cite web |author=Government of Denmark |title=Danish FM Espersen meets President Abbas in Copenhagen |url=http://www.ambdamaskus.um.dk/en/menu/TheEmbassy/News/DanishFMEspersenMeetsPresidentAbbasICopenhagen.htm?printmode=True |date=10 March 2011 |publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs |access-date=1 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006095358/http://www.ambdamaskus.um.dk/en/menu/TheEmbassy/News/DanishFMEspersenMeetsPresidentAbbasICopenhagen.htm?printmode=True |archive-date=6 October 2011}}</ref> During the campaign for the 2011 [[2011 Danish parliamentary election|elections]], the largest opposition party argued that Denmark should recognize the State of Palestine. Foreign Minister [[Lene Espersen]] warned that such a unilateral decision could have "more negative than beneficial" consequences, and stressed the need to co-ordinate policy with the EU.<ref>{{cite news |agency=Agence France-Presse |title=Denmark to recognize Palestine if Social Democrats win polls, report says |url=http://www.nowlebanon.com/NewsArchiveDetails.aspx?ID=272645 |date=19 May 2011 |newspaper=NOW Lebanon |access-date=1 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915080249/http://www.nowlebanon.com/NewsArchiveDetails.aspx?ID=272645 |archive-date=15 September 2012 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> In December 2014, a bill that called on Denmark to recognize Palestine as a state was rejected in the Danish parliament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thelocal.dk/20141212/denmark-votes-against-recognizing-palestine/|title=Denmark votes against recognizing Palestine|date=12 December 2014|publisher=thelocal.dk|access-date=5 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205005118/https://www.thelocal.dk/20141212/denmark-votes-against-recognizing-palestine/|url-status=live}}</ref> In July 2025, Foreign Minister [[Lars Løkke Rasmussen]] responded to the planned recognition of Palestine by France, stating that Denmark preferred such recognition to stem from a negotiated two-state solution or a coordinated EU effort.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 July 2025 |title=Løkke har ikke planer om at følge i Frankrigs fodspor lige nu |trans-title=Løkke has no plans to follow in France's footsteps right now |url=https://www.dr.dk/nyheder/udland/live-israel-angriber-iran?focusId=9933336 |access-date=25 July 2025 |work=[[DR (broadcaster)|DR]] |language=da}}</ref> In August 2025, Prime Minister [[Mette Frederiksen]] announced that Denmark would not recognize Palestine at this time because "it will not help the thousands of children who are currently fighting for their survival, no matter how much we might wish it."<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 August 2025 |title=Denmark will not recognize Palestine, says Mette Frederiksen |url=https://cphpost.dk/2025-08-16/news/politics/denmark-will-not-recognize-palestine-says-mette-frederiksen/ |work=[[The Copenhagen Post]] |access-date=26 August 2025}}</ref> On 22 September 2025, Rasmussen stated Denmark would recognise Palestine after several conditions are met, including all hostages being released, disarming of Hamas, reforming of the Palestinian Authority, and Hamas having no role in the governance of Gaza in the future.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 September 2025 |title=Frankrike har erkänt Palestina: "Det är dags för fred nu" |trans-title=France has recognized Palestine: "It is time for peace now" |url=https://yle.fi/a/7-10084812 |access-date=22 September 2025 |website=Svenska Yle |language=sv-FI}}</ref>|| Yes || EU, NATO; [[Denmark–Palestine relations]]
|-
| {{flag|Eritrea}} || Eritrea is one of only two African countries that do not recognize Palestine, the other being Cameroon.<ref name="erekat" /><ref>{{cite web |author=Government of Ethiopia |title=Democracy in Eritrea? Three generations away says President Isaias |url=http://www.mfa.gov.et/Press_Section/Week_Horn_Africa_October_15_2010.htm |work=A Week in the Horn |publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs |date=15 October 2010 |access-date=15 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928101735/http://www.mfa.gov.et/Press_Section/Week_Horn_Africa_October_15_2010.htm |archive-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> In October 2010, President [[Isaias Afewerki]] stated, "Israel needs a government, we must respect this. The Palestinians also need to have a dignified life, but it can not be the West Bank or Gaza. A two-state solution will not work. It's just to fool people. Israelis and Palestinians living in the same nation will never happen for many reasons. One option that may work is a [[Three-state solution|Transjordan]]. Israel may be left in peace and the Palestinian and Jordanian peoples are brought together and can create their own nation."<ref>{{cite news |last=Boström |first=Daniel |date=11 October 2010 |title=Jag har aldrig ägnat mig åt den frågan |trans-title=I have never addressed that issue |url=http://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/dawitisaak/article7933904.ab |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018025253/http://www.aftonbladet.se/nyheter/dawitisaak/article7933904.ab |archive-date=18 October 2013 |access-date=15 August 2011 |newspaper=Aftonbladet |language=sv}} Translation at [http://hrc-eritrea.org/?p=131 Human Rights Concern Eritrea] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902214148/http://hrc-eritrea.org/?p=131|date=2 September 2011}}. Retrieved 15 August 2011.</ref> In his address to the UN General Assembly in 2011, Isaias stated that "Eritrea reaffirms its long-standing support to the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and an independent, sovereign state. It also upholds the right of Israel to live in peace and security within internationally recognized boundaries."<ref>{{cite web |title=President Isaias Afwerki's Speech at the 66th UN General Assembly |url=http://www.tesfanews.net/archives/3979|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011125355/http://tesfanews.net/archives/3979|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 October 2011 |date=24 September 2011 |access-date=29 November 2012 |publisher=TesfaNews}}</ref> On 29 November 2012, Eritrea voted in favour of a resolution to make Palestine a non-member observer state at the UN. On 23 September 2024, the Minister for Foreign affairs H. E. Osman Saleh emphasized the Palestinians' right to self-determination.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 September 2024 |title=Statement by H.E. Osman Saleh, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Eritrea at the Non-Aligned Movement Ministerial Meeting 23rd September 2024, New York |url=https://shabait.com/2024/09/24/statement-by-h-e-osman-saleh-minister-of-foreign-affairs-of-the-state-of-eritrea-at-the-non-aligned-movement-ministerial-meeting-23rd-september-2024-new-york/ |access-date=21 September 2025 |website=Eritrea Ministry Of Information}}</ref> On 19 January 2025, the Ministry of Information released a press statement welcoming a [[January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire|ceasefire]] in the Gaza war implemented that day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 January 2025 |title=PRESS STATEMENT |url=https://shabait.com/2025/01/19/press-statement-65/ |access-date=21 September 2025 |website=Eritrea Ministry Of Information}}</ref>
| Yes<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tesfanews.net/palestinian-un-bid-for-independence-and-eritrea/ |title=Palestinian UN Bid for Independence and Eritrea |date=22 September 2011 |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=8 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308215513/https://tesfanews.net/palestinian-un-bid-for-independence-and-eritrea/ |url-status=live }}</ref>|| AU
|-
| {{flag|Estonia}} || During a meeting with Riyad al-Malki in June 2010, Minister [[Urmas Paet]] said the country approved an agreement between the two countries and "self-determination for Palestine".<ref>{{cite web |author=Government of Estonia |title=Foreign Minister Paet: Estonia Supports Right to Self-Determination for Palestine |url=http://www.vm.ee/?q=en/node/9638 |date=17 June 2010 |publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs |access-date=7 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120614135033/http://www.vm.ee/?q=en%2Fnode%2F9638 |archive-date=14 June 2012 }}</ref> Officials stated that the government would not adopt a position regarding the UN bid until the final wording of the resolution was published.<ref>{{cite news |author=Kahar |first=Andres |date=8 September 2011 |title=Estonia Remains Wait-and-See on 'Palestinian Question' |url=http://news.err.ee/politics/62414719-e29b-41a7-8240-b671af7306ef |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325071128/http://news.err.ee/politics/62414719-e29b-41a7-8240-b671af7306ef |archive-date=25 March 2012 |access-date=8 September 2011 |newspaper=Eesti Rahvusringhääling}}</ref> On 30 July 2025, Estonian prime minister [[Kristen Michal]] emphasized that Estonia has no plans to recognize Palestine.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prime minister: Estonia has no plans to recognize Palestine |url=https://news.err.ee/1609759785/prime-minister-estonia-has-no-plans-to-recognize-palestine |website=ERR |access-date=31 July 2025 |language=en |date=31 July 2025}}</ref>|| Yes<ref name="Estonia">{{cite web |author=Government of Estonia |title=Diplomatic relations |url=http://www.vm.ee/?q=en/node/9975 |publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs |access-date=20 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102005156/http://www.vm.ee/?q=en%2Fnode%2F9975 |archive-date=2 January 2011 }}</ref>|| EU, NATO
|-
| {{flag|Fiji}} || Fijian policy on the Israeli–Palestinian conflict is largely based on UN resolutions.<ref>{{cite web |author=Government of Fiji |title=Hansard for Friday, 24 May 2002 |url=http://www.parliament.gov.fj/hansard/viewhansard.aspx?hansardID=607&viewtype=full |publisher=House of Representatives |date=24 May 2002 |access-date=29 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927072756/http://www.parliament.gov.fj/hansard/viewhansard.aspx?hansardID=607&viewtype=full |archive-date=27 September 2011}}</ref>|| No || MSG, PIF
|-
| {{flag|Finland}} || Finland supports a two-state solution to the conflict.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://valtioneuvosto.fi/en/-/statement-by-finland-on-recent-events-in-the-middle-east|title=Statement by Finland on Recent Events in the Middle East|website=Valtioneuvosto|access-date=15 March 2022|archive-date=15 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315004422/https://valtioneuvosto.fi/en/-/statement-by-finland-on-recent-events-in-the-middle-east|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2025, President [[Alexander Stubb]] stated that he is willing to approve recognition of Palestine if the government presses forward with such a proposal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 August 2025 |title=Finnish president says he is ready to OK Palestine recognition if government goes ahead with move |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/finnish-president-says-he-is-ready-to-ok-palestine-recognition-if-government-goes-ahead-with-move/ |work=The Times of Israel |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref> Prime Minister [[Petteri Orpo]] stated that Finland is not preparing to recognize Palestine.<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 August 2025 |title=Finland not moving to recognise Palestine |url=https://yle.fi/a/74-20176646 |work=[[Yle]] |access-date=11 August 2025}}</ref> In September 2025, he announced a set of conditions before recognition would be implemented.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tara |date=2025-09-30 |title=Orpo sets conditions for recognising Palestine amid heated debate in parliament |url=https://www.helsinkitimes.fi/finland/finland-news/politics/28059-orpo-sets-conditions-for-recognising-palestine-amid-heated-debate-in-parliament.html |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=Helsinki Times |language=en-gb}}</ref>|| Yes || EU, NATO; [[Finland–Palestine relations]]
|-
| {{flag|Germany}} || In April 2011, Chancellor [[Angela Merkel]] labelled the Palestinian bid for recognition a "unilateral step",<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marx |first1=Bettina |last2=Scheschkewitz |first2=Daniel |date=26 July 2011 |title=Palestinian independence plans unlikely to succeed |url=http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,15267617,00.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812134331/http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,15267617,00.html |archive-date=12 August 2011 |access-date=15 August 2011 |publisher=Deutsche Welle}}</ref> and stated unequivocally that Germany will not recognize a Palestinian state without its prior acceptance by Israel, "Unilateral recognitions therefore definitely do not contribute to achieving this aim ... This is our stance now and it will be our stance in September. There needs to be mutual recognition, otherwise it is not a two-state solution."<ref>{{cite news |author=Connor |first=Richard |date=7 April 2011 |title=Merkel will not recognize unilaterally-declared Palestinian state |url=https://www.dw.com/en/merkel-will-not-recognize-unilaterally-declared-palestinian-state/a-14974756 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120121072147/http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,14974756,00.html |archive-date=21 January 2012 |access-date=15 August 2011 |publisher=Deutsche Welle}}</ref> She also reaffirmed her government's commitment to see an agreement reached as soon as possible, "We want a two-state solution. We want to recognize a Palestinian state. Let us ensure that negotiations begin. It is urgent."<ref>{{cite news |agency=Agence France-Presse |title=Merkel plays down French rift over Palestine |url=http://www.thelocal.de/politics/20110506-34837.html |date=6 May 2011 |newspaper=The Local |access-date=15 August 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131018040537/http://www.thelocal.de/politics/20110506-34837.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In August 2025, Chancellor [[Friedrich Merz]] said Germany would not recognize Palestine as it does not "see the requirements met".<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 August 2025 |title=Merz: Germany will not join allies' initiative to recognise Palestinian state |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/merz-germany-will-not-join-allies-initiative-recognise-palestinian-state-2025-08-26/ |access-date=20 September 2025 |work=Reuters}}</ref>
{{show
|Further details
|
The [[East Germany|German Democratic Republic]] recognized the State of Palestine on 18 November 1988,<ref name="unesco"/> but it later [[German reunification|unified]] with the [[West Germany|Federal Republic of Germany]] and the current government does not recognize it.}}
| Yes || EU, G7, G20, NATO; [[Germany–Palestine relations]]
|-
| {{flag|Greece}} || Under previous governments, Greece garnered a reputation as a staunch supporter of the Palestinian cause.<ref>{{cite book |author=Government of Israel |chapter=Introduction |title=Greece's Relations with Israel, 1961–1967|chapter-url=https://www.archives.gov.il/archivegov_eng/publications/electronicpirsum/greece/introduction1.htm |publisher=Israel State Archives |series=Documents on the Foreign Policy of Israel |access-date=15 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006094718/http://www.archives.gov.il/archivegov_eng/publications/electronicpirsum/greece/introduction1.htm |archive-date=6 October 2011 }}</ref> Within the wider Arab–Israeli conflict, [[Andreas Papandreou]] maintained a stronger stand against Israel than any other government in the European Community. Diplomatic relations were founded with the PLO in 1981, while relations with Israel were maintained only at the consular level until Greece's formal recognition of Israel in 1990 under [[Konstantinos Mitsotakis]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Kaminaris |first=S.C. |date=June 1999 |title=Greece and the Middle East |url=http://meria.idc.ac.il/journal/1999/issue2/jv3n2a4.html |url-status=dead |journal=Middle East Review of International Affairs |publisher=Rubin, Barry; Global Research in International Affairs |volume=3 |issue=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907015834/http://meria.idc.ac.il/journal/1999/issue2/jv3n2a4.html |archive-date=7 September 2011 |access-date=15 August 2011}}</ref> Since the formation of current foreign policy under [[George Papandreou]], Greece has seen a rapid improvement in relations with Israel,<ref>{{cite news |last=Marcus |first=Jonathan |date=16 October 2010 |title=Israel woos Greece after rift with Turkey |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-11556442 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829144740/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-11556442 |archive-date=29 August 2019 |access-date=15 August 2011 |work=BBC News}}</ref> leading the media to mark the conclusion of Greece's pro-Palestinian era.<ref>{{cite news |last=Athanasiadis |first=Iason |title=A Mediterranean Battlefield |url=http://www.majalla.com/eng/2011/01/article1992 |newspaper=Al Majalla |date=31 January 2011 |access-date=15 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714231233/http://www.majalla.com/eng/2011/01/article1992 |archive-date=14 July 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In December 2015, Greece's parliament voted in favour of a motion requesting that the government recognize Palestine.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/greek-parliament-votes-to-recognize-palestinian-state-1450783327 |title=Greek Parliament Recognizes Palestinian State in Symbolic Vote |date=22 December 2015 |access-date=22 December 2015 |last=Stamouli |first=Nektaria |newspaper=The Wall Street Journal |archive-date=17 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201117044958/https://www.wsj.com/articles/greek-parliament-votes-to-recognize-palestinian-state-1450783327 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 7 September 2025, Prime Minister [[Kyriakos Mitsotakis]] declared that Greece will recognize Palestinian statehood at the right time.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Giannopoulos |first=Bill |date=7 September 2025 |title=PM: Greece to Recognize Palestinian State at Appropriate Time |url=https://greekcitytimes.com/2025/09/08/pm-greece-to-recognize-palestinian-state-at-appropriate-time/ |work=Greek City Times |access-date=8 September 2025}}</ref>|| Yes || EU, NATO; [[Greece–Palestine relations]]
|-
